summary: Responds to SEBI's move to extend derivative tenures: argues expiry-day extra margin should apply to daily intraday, not positional traders; wants covered calls margin-free, 9-month penalty removed, exposure margin dropped for 2-month-plus positions, and long-dated stock options/futures introduced.
lessons: Span margin equals maximum risk plus exposure margin; an option buyer pays only premium (max risk known) while a seller pays ~50,000 for a 10,000-rupee max-risk position - exposure margin is a policy choice, not a risk measure.

If the goal is moving traders from short-dated frenzy to long-dated calm, penalize intraday daily (not just expiry days) and reward long tenure by removing the 9-month extra margin and exposure margin.
A covered call against shares in demat is zero-risk; charging full margin on it discourages exactly the hedging SEBI says it wants.

India offers Nifty options to 5 years but stock options only 3 months with poor liquidity; long-dated stock options and futures would let investors earn premium on holdings, as US covered-call practice shows.
Calendar-spread traders are the lowest-risk participants, yet they lose margin benefit on expiry days - the deterrent lands on the wrong crowd.

summary: Builds a zero-downside HNI portfolio: buy Nifty BeES (~20 lakh per lot-equivalent), buy far-dated 25,000PE and sell 28,000CE for equal premium - a zero-cost collar; worst case ~0, best case ~13-14% to Dec-2026; ladder averaging every further 5% fall using debt-fund money.
lessons: Buy 100:1 Nifty BeES to one options lot; the ETF trades ~40-45 points above fair value because it retains dividends - the same premium applies when you sell, so it nets out.

A collar funded by equal premiums (buy 25,000PE, sell 28,000CE on Dec-2026) gives zero downside and ~3,400 points of capped upside (~13-14% over ~17 months) - slightly better than FD with full protection.

Because the protected position cannot lose, you can ladder new collars every further 5% of market fall using debt-fund tranches (20% at -10%, then each -5%) - courage without conviction-destroying drawdowns.
Nifty has not fallen 30% in 25 years except COVID and Lehman, and both times markets more than doubled within about a year - the ladder's stop condition.
India charges span + exposure + extra >9-month margin even on hedged ETF positions, where the US charges nothing for covered calls - friction that keeps zero-risk capital out of the market.

summary: Nifty is down 2-3% over a year while every major market sits near all-time highs - a local, not global, decline. A US appeals court ruled most Trump tariffs illegal with a stay to Oct 14 for Supreme Court appeal - headline relief, but economists note alternate legal routes keep the effective tariff alive.
For a foreign investor, a 7-8% rupee fall turns a flat year into a -10% year; currency defense, not slogans, is the missing policy tool.
